newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - 24 March 1997.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - 24 March 1997.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

A potential jail break has been foiled at Northern Ireland's notorious Maze prison. The escape tunnel discovered last night led from block H7 which is occupied by Provisional IRA inmates and was the location of the 1983 escape.
-- WORLD MARKETS WAIT FOR GREENSPAN MOVE

Tomorrow the Federal Market Open Committee meet to decide the outcome of US interest rates. Attention is focused on the Chairman of the Federal Reserve, Alan Greenspan. Speculation is moving heavily in favour of a rise of between 0.25 and 0.5 percentage points.
-- HANBO PROBE TAKES IN PRESIDENT'S SON

As part of a renewed probe into the loan scandal surrounding the collapse of Hanbo group, the second son of South Korean President is being investigated. Kim HyunChul is alleged to have taken a bribe worth 140mn stg from a businessmen acting on behalf of HAnbo.
-- HK STAFF EXCEL IN TELECOM COST CUTS

The Hong Kong Telecommunications Company, a subsidiary of Cable & Wireless, is actively pursuing a new business strategy called Operation Excel, in which employees are invited to suggest ideas for cutting costs. One such idea involves staff delivering telephone bills during their time off.
-- FIESTY FIGHTER WHO LIT UP THE TOBACCO WORLD
A profile of Bennett S LeBow, the man who has forged a settlement for tobacco company the Liggett group.
